To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PPARγ is decreased in children with obesity and may be associated with diminished plasma ANGPTI4 levels.
PPARγ gene is down-regulated in obese subjects as well as in children with IR.

PPARγ expression in PBMCs and plasma ANGPTl4 levels were significantly decreased in children and adolescents with obese compared to those with normal weight and were not significantly different between obese with or without IR or metabolic syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PPARγ in obesity and its association with IR and ANGPTI4 levels.
the role of PPARγ and its downstream target ANGPTL in obesity and IR in children.
the relationship between PPARγ gene in PBMCs and plasma ANGPT L4 levels in obese subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PPARγ expression is significantly decreased in obese children and this decrease may be responsible for decreased ANGPTL-4 levels.
PPARγ expression in PBMCs and ANGPTl4 in plasma are significantly decreased in obese children and may be involved in the pathogenesis of obesity and related complications.
PPARγ is down-regulated in obesity and that ANGPTL 4 may be one of the downstream genes that are affected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PPARγ is a potential therapeutic target in obesity.
the PPARγ/ANGPTL4 axis is involved in obesity and may play an important role in the development of obesity and related metabolic complications.
PPARγ is a potential therapeutic target for treatment of metabolic syndrome in childhood obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PPARγ gene may be a potential biomarker for childhood obesity and metabolic syndrome.
PPARγ expression in PBMCs may be used as an indicator for the presence of metabolic syndrome.
the expression of PPARγ and its downstream target ANGPTL-4 are altered in obese children and may be associated with metabolic parameters.
